title: Smooth connected relative commutator subgroup and its minimality
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine [def-pc-scheme] $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with closed subgroup schemes as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $G$ be smooth and connected and let $N\subseteq G$ be a smooth connected normal closed subgroup. There exists a smooth connected normal closed subgroup $D\subseteq G$ contained in $N$ such that, for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, every $g\in G(R)$ and every $n\in N(R)$, one has $gng^{-1}n^{-1}\in D(R)$. If $K\subseteq G$ is any closed subgroup scheme such that $gng^{-1}n^{-1}\in K(R)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, every $g\in G(R)$ and every $n\in N(R)$, then $D\subseteq K$. The subgroup $K$ need not be smooth, connected or normal. Denote this smallest subgroup by $[G,N]$.

source.place: Definition 6.24 and Remark 6.25(b), printed p.131; generated-subgroup construction and scalar extension, Propositions 2.46–2.48 and 2.50, printed pp.54–56; normality and containment for [G,N] with N normal, as used in the descending central series preceding Proposition 6.38, printed p.133.

proof.text: Put $X=G\times_kN$, $o=(e,e)$ and $A=k[G]$. The affine-product identification [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] makes $X$ and its powers affine. The finite-type base-change and composition clauses of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] show that $X$ and all its powers are of finite type over $k$. We will use the following elementary affine test throughout: for an affine $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and a closed subscheme $K=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ of $G$, a morphism $u:Y\to G$ factors through $K$ precisely when $u^*(J)=0$. Indeed the homomorphism $u^*:A\to B$ then descends to $A/J$, and conversely a descended homomorphism kills $J$. Equivalently one may test membership in $K(B)$ of the universal point $u_B(\mathrm{id}_B)$. The descriptions of affine morphisms and closed subschemes used here are [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Propositions 2.46–2.48, pp.54–55, affine setup; finite-type products: Stacks Tags 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type), 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type)

proof.text:
The group operations [def-sc-group-scheme] define the morphism $c:X\to G$, $c(g,n)=gng^{-1}n^{-1}$, and $c(o)=e$. Normality of $N$ in the sense of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] gives $gng^{-1}\in N(R)$ for every $R$, hence $c(g,n)\in N(R)$. The image of $c$ is inversion stable on every algebra, since
$$c(g,n)^{-1}=ngn^{-1}g^{-1}=c(g^{-1},gng^{-1}),$$
and the second entry on the right lies in $N(R)$. The same normality, tested on the universal point of the affine scheme $G\times_kN$ using step 1, gives a morphism $G\times_kN\to N$, $(h,n)\mapsto hnh^{-1}$. Thus all subsequent conjugation substitutions are morphisms, not merely substitutions of geometric points.

source.place: Definition 6.24 and Remark 6.25(b), p.131; relative commutator calculation for normal N

proof.text: The projection $X\to N$ is the base change of the smooth morphism $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change] makes it smooth. Its composite with the smooth structure morphism of $N$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Hence $X$ is geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied over the field $k$. The base is a field and both group schemes are smooth by hypothesis; no perfection hypothesis on $k$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 2.48 and 2.50, pp.55–56, geometric reducedness input; Stacks Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 01VA (lemma-composition-smooth), 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal)

proof.text: The identity sections give $k$-rational points of the connected schemes $G$ and $N$. Apply [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] separately to their structure morphisms: $G$ and $N$ are geometrically connected. For every field extension $L/k$, $G_L$ is again geometrically connected (any further extension is an extension of $k$), and $N_L$ is nonempty and connected. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] over $L$: the components of $G_L\times_LN_L=X_L$ are in bijection with those of $N_L$. Thus $X_L$ has exactly one component and is nonempty, also witnessed by $o_L$. This proves geometric connectedness of $X$.

Apply [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup] to $(G,X,o,c)$. The affineness and finite-type conditions are step 1, and its pointedness and inversion-stability conditions are step 2. With $w_n:X^n\to G$ the product of $n$ commutators and $I=\bigcap_{n\geq1}\ker(w_n^*)$, it gives the closed subgroup $j:D=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow G$ through which $c$ factors, minimal among all closed subgroups through which $c$ factors. It is affine of finite type, geometrically reduced by step 3 and geometrically connected by step 4. Apply [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] to this finite-type group scheme to deduce smoothness. In particular $D$ is connected (take the extension $k/k$). Write $C=A/I$, $B_n=k[X^n]$ and $f_n:C\to B_n$ for the induced pullbacks of the word maps. Directly from the formula for $I$, if all $f_n(z)$ vanish then $z=0$.

source.place: Propositions 2.46 and 2.48, pp.54–55; Proposition 2.50, p.56; Definition 6.24 and Remark 6.25(b), p.131

proof.text: Since $c$ factors through $D$, evaluation gives $c(g,n)\in D(R)$ for every $R,g,n$ in the statement. Conversely let $K\subseteq G$ be any closed subgroup containing all those commutators on all $k$-algebras. Taking $R=k[X]$ and the universal point of $X$ shows by the affine test of step 1 that $c$ factors through $K$. Minimality in [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup] gives $D\subseteq K$. This uses no smoothness, connectedness or normality of $K$. Apply the same argument to $K=N$, using the membership proved in step 2, to obtain $D\subseteq N$.

source.place: Proposition 2.46, pp.54–55; Definition 6.24, p.131; containment used in the descending central series preceding Proposition 6.38, p.133

proof.text:
Consider the morphism $q:G\times_kD\to G$, $q(h,d)=hdh^{-1}$. For each $n$ define $T_n:G\times_kX^n\to X^n$ by simultaneously replacing each pair $(g_i,n_i)$ by $(hg_ih^{-1},hn_ih^{-1})$. These are morphisms by the conjugation morphism from step 2 and the group operations [def-sc-group-scheme]. Cancellation in any group gives
$$h\,c(g_i,n_i)h^{-1}=c(hg_ih^{-1},hn_ih^{-1}),$$
so $q\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times\bar w_n)=w_n\circ T_n$, where $\bar w_n:X^n\to D$ is the factorization from step 5. Consequently for every $a\in I$, the pullback of $q^*(a)$ along $\mathrm{id}_G\times\bar w_n$ is $T_n^*w_n^*(a)=0$. The affine-product identification [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] expresses this as
$$(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes f_n)(q^*(a))=0,\qquad q^*(a)\in A\otimes_kC.$$

source.place: Definition 6.24, p.131, conjugation of relative commutator words; compare the normality argument of Proposition 6.18, p.129

proof.text: The maps $f_n:C\to B_n$ jointly detect zero by step 5. Swap the two tensor factors of $q^*(a)$ and apply [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection] with $M=C$, $N=A$ and the family $(f_n)_{n\geq1}$. Step 7 gives all its required vanishing equations; hence $q^*(a)=0$ for every $a\in I$. The affine test from step 1 therefore factors $q$ through $D$. On $R$-points this says $hD(R)h^{-1}\subseteq D(R)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $h\in G(R)$. Applying the same inclusion to $h^{-1}$ gives equality. Thus $D$ is normal by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Combined with steps 5 and 6 this proves every asserted property; the minimality makes $D$ unique and defines $[G,N]$.

source.place: Proposition 2.46, pp.54–55, tensor detection for word maps; Definition 6.24 and Remark 6.25(b), p.131; normality as used before Proposition 6.38, p.133
